paraphrase: In the Lokāyatika view the principles are four elements only; consciousness arises from them like intoxicating power from ingredients, the self being known in 'I am fat', 'I am thin'; pleasure born of embraces is the human aim, pain from thorns is hell; the lord is the king known to the world; liberation is the body's destruction, not knowledge; perception alone is a means of knowledge.
notes: Reported by an opponent: the Sarvasiddhāntasaṅgraha ascribed to Śaṅkara (Advaita doxography). Chapter and exact verse set from memory; the same verses are quoted in a modern Sanskrit history in sources_raw under the doubtful title 'Cārvākaṣaṣṭi'.
